chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-'Abbas b. Ma'ruf, from Ali b. Mahziyar, from al-Husayn b. Sa'id, from Ali b. al-Nu'man, from Dawud b. Farqad. He said: I heard my father asking Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him):

When does the time of Maghrib begin? He said: When its seat disappears. He said: And what is its seat? He said: Its disk. He said: When does its disk disappear? He said: When you look and do not see it.

key_terms.المغرب: Maghrib — the sunset prayer, one of the five daily obligatory prayers
key_terms.قرصها: Its disk — refers to the round disk of the sun as it appears at the horizon
key_terms.كرسيها: Its seat/pedestal — metaphorical term for the sun's visible disk or the lower portion resting on the horizon

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Maghrib prayer begin according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this legal hadith, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the precise timing for the onset of Maghrib prayer. When asked about when Maghrib time enters, the Imam uses the term 'kursi' (seat/pedestal) of the sun, then explains it means the sun's disk (qurs). The criterion is complete disappearance of the sun's disk below the horizon, determined simply by looking and no longer being able to see it. This practical definition was important for early Muslims who relied on direct observation rather than calculated timetables.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-`Abbas b. Ma`ruf from `Ali b. Mahzayar from al-Husayn b. Sa`id from `Ali b. al-Nu`man from Dawud b. Farqad. He said: I heard my father ask Aba `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as):

When does Maghrib time begin? So, he said: When its seat disappears. He said: What is its seat? He said: Its disk. He said: When does its disk disappear? He said: If you look to it, you do not see it.
